Firstly, you should see the actual curriculum of physics and chemistry followed in engineering streams. It is not always similar to the physics and chemistry taught in high school. Different Streams of engineering are focused on different aspects of Physics and Chemistry. You might not like the actual topics covered in these degrees. Secondly, Try to imagine yourself working with a degree in your desired field. Will you be able to work in that environment? Will you be happy with a profession in that engineering stream? Will you be happy in the profession? If your answer was yes to these questions, then you already know which field to choose. Thirdly, perform some research on the scope of your chosen field of engineering in the future. If the scope is not much, Please try not to go for it. For example, the field of Petrochemical engineering is expected to have very less scope in future due to inclination of world towards renewable energy. Fourthly, consider the amount of competition in your chosen field of engineering before finalizing it. For example, the field of Computer engineering is becoming saturated with every passing year, even though there is a massive increase in employment opportunities in that field. Finally, i would like to say that you can excel in any field of engineering, given that you are passionate about it and ready to work hard

Question: Have you ever caught a teacher purposely taking points off your grade for no reason?
Answer: It was my seventh grade teacher. Lets call her Mrs. X. She had just started teaching physics to us. I was one of the toppers for class who could easily get 98 out of hundred on an exam. I was one of the brilliant kids in my class who had never received low marks. Mrs. X, for some or the other reason, was a bit too strict. One day we had a test in physics. The test was easy and I was expecting a 9 out of 10. It was a piece of cake. I knew that all my answers were correct. The test was on Monday. So we waited for the results. We were a total of 11 students in our class. On Tuesday, Mrs. X entered the class with the result. One by one she distributed the results. Then she came to my desk and gave my result with a wicked face. I WAS SHOCKED AT THE RESULT. I had gotten a 0.5 out of 10. My mind went numb for a couple of minutes. Then I turned around and found the same look on everyone’s faces. Let me tell you the marks of the class. 1 girl (let’s call her Tina) got 8. 4 students (including me) got 0.5. The 6 remaining students got a 0, a goddamn zero. We were all shocked. We asked her what had gone wrong. Her reply, “Go and check your answers with Tina.” After cross-checking, I found no difference, no difference at all. We all protested but nothing happened. In the recess all of us (excluding Tina) went to the principal to complain but this was also futile. Next day all our parents came to school and had a long discussion. Fortunately Mrs. X never came to school after that.
